briefings.title: AI for Chip Design & Chip Design for AI | Ricursive Intelligence | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Ricursive Intelligence is automating end-to-end chip design using a dual-loop AI architecture—combining proprietary inner-loop optimization tools with outer-loop LLMs—to accelerate development and usher in a "designless era" of workload-tailored custom silicon.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Ricursive Intelligence is automating end-to-end chip design using a dual-loop AI architecture—combining proprietary inner-loop optimization tools with outer-loop LLMs—to accelerate development and usher in a "designless era" of workload-tailored custom silicon.

## Company Background & Foundations
- **Founding Team & Origins:** Founded by Anna Goldie (CEO) and Azalia Mirhoseini (CTO), who met on their first day at Google Brain in 2016 and later led the Machine Learning for Systems team.
- **The AlphaChip Precursor:** Created AlphaChip, a deep reinforcement learning agent generating superhuman chip layouts in hours instead of weeks/months.
- **Industry Deployment:** Deployed across Google's last four generations of TPUs, Axion CPUs, Pixel phones, Waymo chips, and externally by MediaTek.

## Three-Phase Company Roadmap
- **Phase One (Current):** Accelerate traditional chip design from 1+ years to drastically shorter timeframes by overhauling physical design and verification for chipmakers like Nvidia, AMD, and Intel.
- **Phase Two (Democratization / "Designless Era"):** Enable application and frontier AI labs (such as those building models like Claude) to bypass the traditional hardware lottery by using Ricursive as a platform to co-design computer architectures tailored to specific new workloads.
- **Phase Three (Recursive Self-Improvement):** Build proprietary chips, train proprietary models, co-evolve them, and close the recursive self-improving loop.

## Technical Approach: The Dual-Loop Architecture
- **Dual-Loop Optimization:** 
  - *Inner Loop:* Proprietary optimization tools (like a static timing analysis engine) running 100x to 1,000x faster than traditional commercial tools with 0.999+ correlation to actual tools, executing in seconds or milliseconds.
  - *Outer Loop:* An LLM that leverages the high-speed inner loop to perform agentic optimization, tuning parameters, and even rewriting tools to optimize metrics such as wire length.
- **End-to-End Scope:** Automating the entire workflow from architectural design and exploration down to GDS2 (the format sent to fabs like TSMC).
- **Customization Impact:** Focusing on high-consequence microarchitecture decisions—such as systolic array dimensions and memory hierarchy organization—which yield multiplier performance improvements and Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) gains compared to downstream physical layout optimization (which yields ~20% power improvement).

## Team Composition & Expertise
- **Multidisciplinary Talent:** The team includes engineers who worked on frontier AI models (Claude, Gemini, Grok) alongside silicon experts who built iPhone chips and Google TPUs.
- **Academic Ties:** Co-founder Azalia Mirhoseini serves as a faculty member at Stanford University, where related research on AI compilers (replacing compiler stacks like PyTorch-to-PTX) has been conducted.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Custom Chip Proliferation:** The scale of AI deployment across robotics, self-driving cars, AR/VR, and space exploration will drive massive growth in custom chips tailored to diverse AI form factors — *Azalia Mirhoseini & Anna Goldie*
- **The Designless Era:** Application companies will increasingly skip building massive in-house teams of hundreds or thousands of chip design experts, instead outsourcing custom silicon creation to platforms like Ricursive — *Azalia Mirhoseini*

## Notable Quotes
> *"Chips are the fuel for intelligence and they're basically the silicon substrate for AI and we can we need to use AI to design better chips to fuel the next generation of AI models and close this recursive self-improving loop."* — **Anna Goldie**

> *"Just like TSMC and other fabs enabled the fabless era, where companies like Nvidia and Apple could focus on the design process... we want to unlock the designless era."* — **Azalia Mirhoseini**

briefings.title: AMD Advancing AI 2026: Lisa Su Full Keynote
briefings.tldr: AMD CEO Dr. Lisa Su outlined the company's 2026 AI vision at Advancing AI, announcing the production launch of the Helios AI rack, the Venice (Zen 6) server CPU family, and expanding multi-billion-dollar partnerships with OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Cisco, and AT&T.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** AMD CEO Dr. Lisa Su outlined the company's 2026 AI vision at Advancing AI, announcing the production launch of the Helios AI rack, the Venice (Zen 6) server CPU family, and expanding multi-billion-dollar partnerships with OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Cisco, and AT&T.

## Market Outlook & Strategic Forecasts
- **Exploding AI Demand:** Token consumption has surged by nearly 160 times over two years to over 35 quadrillion tokens per month.
- **Inference Over Training:** In 2026, roughly 60% of global AI compute capacity is being used for inference as workloads shift from building models to executing them.
- **Upgraded Market Projections:** 
  - **AI Accelerators:** AMD raised its 2028 market forecast of $500B to **$1.4 trillion by 2030**, approaching the size of today's entire semiconductor market.
  - **Server CPUs:** Driven by agentic AI sandboxes, the server CPU market is projected to grow over 50% to **over $200 billion by 2030** (up from $25B today).
  - **Overall Portfolio:** High-performance and adaptive computing products are expected to grow at a ~40% CAGR, approaching a **$2 trillion market by 2030**.

## Data Center Infrastructure: Helios & Instinct GPUs
- **Helios AI Rack Launch:** In full production with shipments starting late Q3 and ramping in Q4 2026. Tom Brown confirmed Anthropic is deploying up to **2 gigawatts of Helios**, while Satchin Katti confirmed OpenAI will deploy Helios at massive scale starting late 2026 through 2027.
- **Hardware Specs & Metrics:** 
  - **MI455 Accelerator:** Features 320 billion transistors built on TSMC 2nm and 3nm, 12 compute/IO chiplets with 432 GB of HBM4 memory connected via 3D chip-stack packaging.
  - **Performance vs. Competitors:** Helios delivers 15% more compute, 50% more HBM4 capacity/bandwidth, 50% more scale-out bandwidth, and up to **30% more tokens per dollar** at a fixed rack power.
- **Deep Partnerships & Custom Silicon:**
  - **OpenAI:** Satchin Katti noted OpenAI was first to bet on AMD (MI300/350/Helios) and is utilizing AI for automated compiler and kernel optimization.
  - **Meta:** Santosh Janardhan discussed multi-year co-design across 4 generations of EPYC and deployment of MI450 racks across ranking and recommendation systems.
  - **Cerebras:** CEO Andrew Feldman announced a disaggregated low-latency inference solution combining Helios with the Cerebras wafer-scale engine to deliver 5x higher throughput.

## Server CPUs: The Venice (Zen 6) Family
- **Divided Server Workloads:** Compute is splitting into GPU servers (speed/IO), agent sandboxes (density/cores-per-watt), and general-purpose enterprise servers (efficiency/TCO).
- **Venice Family Details:** Built on TSMC's 2nm process with 203 billion transistors and up to 512 threads per socket (Zen 6 core):
  - **Venice HF:** 96-core processor optimized to feed GPU host nodes (up to 5 GHz).
  - **Venice 256-core:** Highest compute density in the industry, built with 8 compute chiplets (32 cores each) for agentic sandboxes.
  - **Venice 128-core:** Tuned for lower-cost, lower-power enterprise and general-purpose workloads.
  - **Future Roadmap:** Verando (next year for AI) and Venice X (utilizing 3D V-Cache stacking for HPC).
- **Performance Benchmarks:** Venice delivers up to **1.8 times more tokens per second** than x86 competitors in GPU servers, **2x more agents per watt** in sandboxes, and **2.8x more agents per watt** than leading ARM processors at the chip level. Venice is in full production with rollouts in Q4.

## Software: ROCm.ai & Agentic Development
- **Vamsi Bopanna (SVP of AI):** Highlighted 6-week release cycles for ROCm and broad open-source adoption (Hugging Face, PyTorch, VLLM).
- **Introduction of ROCm.ai:** An agentic AI platform that turns popular coding agents (Cursor, Claude, Codex) into ROCm superusers for automated GPU programming, kernel generation, and optimization.
- **Hyperloom:** An AI-assisted optimization layer that analyzed 14,000 models to auto-tune configurations and select kernels, yielding a **3.8x speedup over ROCm 7** for DeepSeek and a 2.4x boost for training.
- **OpenAI Software Collaboration:** Philippe Tillet (OpenAI) discussed code-generation collaboration utilizing Triton and Gleon compilers on open-source AMD infrastructure.
- **HPC & Sovereign AI:** The **MI430X** GPU (shipping H1 2027) delivers native FP64 hardware performance (288 teraflops, 9x better than competition) powering exascale sovereign AI factories at Oak Ridge National Labs and in Europe (GENCI/CINES).

## Enterprise, Personal, and Physical AI (Edge)
- **Enterprise AI & AT&T:** 
  - Dan McNamara (SVP, Compute & Enterprise AI) introduced the air-cooled **Instinct MI350P** GPU, supporting up to 260B parameters and delivering **4x more tokens/sec/dollar** for enterprise servers without facility upgrades.
  - Jeremy Legg (CTO, AT&T) noted AT&T processes 1+ trillion tokens/month, announced the open-source **OTel 2.0** telecom model trained on AMD, and highlighted cost reductions via multi-model routing.
- **Personal AI & Cisco:**
  - Jack Huynh (GM, Computing & Graphics) introduced **Ryzen AI Halo** (supporting up to 200B parameters with 120 GB unified memory) and **Gorgon Halo** (up to 300B parameters with 192 GB unified memory).
  - Jeetu Patel (Cisco) detailed the integration of Halo devices with Cisco Cloud Control for unified management, tokenomics monitoring, and security guardrails (GA in early fall).
- **Physical AI & Robotics:** Launched the **AMD Kria AI System on Module** (powered by Ryzen AI Embedded X100) and the Kria AI robotics developer platform, delivering **3.4x better real-time results** and **2.3x more concurrent agents** than competing architectures (Nvidia Jetson Thor).

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Lisa Su:** The AI accelerator market will reach **$1.4 trillion by 2030**.
- **Lisa Su:** The server CPU market will grow over 50% to **over $200 billion by 2030**.
- **Lisa Su:** AMD's high-performance and adaptive computing products will grow at roughly a **40% CAGR over the next several years**, approaching a **$2 trillion market by 2030**.
- **Lisa Su:** MI500 (powering next-gen HBM and optical interconnects) will deliver the largest generational leap in Instinct history, putting AMD on track to deliver **more than 2,000 times higher inference throughput in just four years** (targeting CDNA next architecture with MI600 in 2028).
- **Lisa Su / Roadmap:** A new Helios rack system will be released **every year**, offering predictable multi-year scaling for customers.
- **Dan McNamara:** Nearly **every enterprise next year (2027)** will have some form of agentic deployment.
- **Jeetu Patel:** Cisco Cloud Control management apparatus for enterprise Halo devices will achieve **general availability in the US in early fall**.

## Notable Quotes
> *"As billions of people every day use AI, the workloads shift from building models to putting them to work... In 2026, for the first time, the world is using more AI compute to run models than to train them."* — **Dr. Lisa Su**

> *"Our actual experience was we had one engineer who start doing it... spun up, connected it to Claude, asked it, hey, bring up this machine, left it going over the weekend, and we ended up with a graph of the actual performance of our leading model on it, just going up and up and up."* — **Tom Brown (Anthropic)**

> *"Humans click, but agents swarm... inferencing is not just going to be limited to the data center, inferencing is going to be distributed everywhere."* — **Jeetu Patel (Cisco)**

> *"We are one of the few companies in the world that's actually post-trained a model on AMD and then been able to drive equivalency in terms of performance and accuracy with other more expensive chip sets in the marketplace."* — **Jeremy Legg (AT&T)**

## 1. Data Center AI Infrastructure & Helios Launch
- **Helios AI Rack System:** Announced by Dr. Lisa Su as the industry's highest-performing AI rack, featuring integrated AMD Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs, and Pensando DPUs/NICs.

- **Sovereign & HPC Compute (MI430X):** Highlighted by Vamsi Boppana; features native hardware double precision (FP64) delivering 288 teraflops of FP64 compute (9x the competition) with leadership memory capacity, shipping in H1 2027 to power exascale AI factories at Oak Ridge National Labs and in Europe.
- **Partner Commitments:**
  - **Anthropic:** Tom Brown announced plans to deploy up to two gigawatts of Helios infrastructure.
  - **OpenAI:** Sachin Katti confirmed OpenAI was the first to receive MI455/Helios racks three months prior, with massive-scale deployments slated for late 2026 through 2027, building on their commitment to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD infrastructure.
  - **Meta:** Santosh Janardhan noted Meta's ongoing multi-generation server and GPU deployments (spanning MI300, MI350, and upcoming MI450/450X clusters tied to their 6-gigawatt strategic agreement).

## 2. Server CPUs & The Agentic Era

- **Venice (6th Gen EPYC Family):** Unveiled by Dr. Su as the CPU family designed specifically for agentic AI workloads, leveraging TSMC's 2nm process and Zen 6 cores (203 billion transistors).
  - **Venice HF (AI Host Nodes):** Features 8 compute chiplets (96 cores total) running up to 5 GHz to keep GPUs fully fed; delivers 1.8x more tokens/second than previous-generation Turin.
  - **Venice 256-Core (Agent Sandboxes):** Features up to 512 threads per socket for industry-leading compute density, delivering over 2x more agents per watt compared to competitive X86 and ARM processors.
  - **Venice 128-Core (General Purpose):** Optimized for low-power, cost-effective enterprise workloads.
  - **Future Roadmap:** Verano (next-gen AI host nodes with low-power memory and faster CPU-GPU interconnects) and Venice X (featuring 3D V-Cache memory stacking beneath compute triplets for technical computing) arriving next year.

## 3. Disaggregated Inference with Cerebras Systems
- **Partnership with Cerebras:** Andrew Feldman joined Dr. Su to introduce a joint disaggregated inference solution combining AMD Helios racks (leadership throughput and memory capacity) with Cerebras wafer-scale engines (leadership SRAM and memory bandwidth).
- **Performance & Availability:** Delivers 5x higher throughput while maintaining ultra-low latency, available later in 2026 via the Cerebras Cloud and on-premise deployments.

## 4. Software & AI-Assisted Development (ROCm.ai)
- **ROCm Evolution:** Vamsi Boppana reported release cycles shortened to every six weeks with Day Zero support now standard across Hugging Face, PyTorch, JAX, vLLM, and SGLang.
- **ROCm.ai Platform:** An agentic AI development platform turning coding agents (Cursor, Claude, Codex) into ROCm superusers to generate, profile, and optimize GPU kernels automatically.
  - **HyperLoom:** An AI-assisted optimization layer that analyzes workloads, tunes configurations, and iterates toward performance goals (tested across a suite of 14,000 models).
  - **Performance Gains:** ROCm.ai delivers up to 3.3x speedups on DeepSeek models and a 2.4x boost in training performance via fused flash attention and checkpointing.
- **OpenAI Software Contributions:** Philippe Tillet discussed OpenAI's work with AMD on open-source compiler stacks (LLM code generation) and deep low-level code generation down to assembly scheduling via Triton and Glueon.

## 5. Client, Personal, and Physical AI (Edge & Robotics)
- **Personal AI & Ryzen AI Halo:** Jack Huynh detailed the shift toward personal AI agents running locally on PCs.
  - **Ryzen AI Halo:** Features 128 GB of unified memory supporting models up to 200 billion parameters.
  - **Gorgon Halo:** Expands unified memory to 192 GB and supports models up to 300 billion parameters.
  - **Hugging Face Partnership:** Includes a full year of Hugging Face Pro for every Halo box to provide optimized open models and agentic toolkits.
- **Enterprise Edge Management with Cisco:** Jeetu Patel joined to announce an integrated enterprise solution combining Ryzen AI Halo desk-side computers with Cisco Cloud Control for unified tokenomics monitoring, security guardrails, and device quarantine capabilities (Generally Available in early fall).
- **Physical AI & Kria Robotics:** Introduced the AMD Kria AI System on Module (powered by Ryzen AI Embedded X100) and the Kria AI Robotics Developer Platform (running ROS/ROS 2). In third-party testing against NVIDIA Jetson Thor, Kria delivers 3.4x better real-time results, 2.3x more concurrent agents, and 1.6x more CPU capacity.

- **OpenAI Deployment Timeline:** OpenAI will deploy Helios systems at massive scale starting towards the end of 2026 and accelerating throughout 2027 — Sachin Katti.

briefings.title: Benchmarks vs. Reality: Lessons from 750 Trillion Tokens | Chris Clark, OpenRouter | RAISE 2026
briefings.tldr: Empirical real-world usage data processed across trillions of tokens reveals a stark gap between theoretical model benchmarks and actual production performance, showing that infrastructure reality—such as caching efficiencies, token chattiness, and serving provider bugs—dramatically alters costs and success rates.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Empirical real-world usage data processed across trillions of tokens reveals a stark gap between theoretical model benchmarks and actual production performance, showing that infrastructure reality—such as caching efficiencies, token chattiness, and serving provider bugs—dramatically alters costs and success rates.

## Multi-Model Reality & Adoption Trends
* **Growing Inference Costs:** Inference is rapidly becoming the second-largest operating expense for knowledge companies; while past growth was driven by AI-native companies treating tokens as COGS, 2026 has seen tokens increasingly used directly as headcount replacement and operating expense.
* **The Multi-Model Shift:** Despite periodic market consolidation fears, the AI ecosystem is definitively multi-model, with companies leveraging diverse models based on specific agentic or operational needs.
* **Open-Weight vs. Frontier Gap:** Open-weight models (primarily from Chinese labs) have maintained a remarkably persistent 4-to-6-month lag behind US frontier labs rather than closing the gap via recursive self-improvement.
* **Regional Adoption Variations:** Global regions display distinct adoption curves for open-weight models, influenced by local marginal costs and declining confidence in single-region providers (such as the market removal of Fable).

## Agentic Workloads & The "Glass Slipper" Effect
* **Challenging Cut-Overs:** Transitioning agentic workloads between models is increasingly difficult because models like DeepSeek 4 require different prompting techniques (e.g., specific behavioral feedback) rather than drop-in replacement.
* **Jagged Frontier Intelligence:** Models scoring higher on theoretical intelligence benchmarks (e.g., Kimmy K26) do not automatically see higher adoption than models optimized specifically for long-horizon agentic workflows (e.g., DeepSeek 4).
* **The Glass Slipper Effect:** Initial cohort users of a model who successfully deploy an agent tend to stick with that specific model long-term ("the shoe fits") and freeze at that point of intelligence rather than constantly migrating to newer models.
* **Two Agent Paradigms:** Builders must choose between two strategies:
  * *Stable Agents:* Workloads where a model is proven to work in production, shifting focus to reliability and cost reduction.
  * *Frontier-Chasing Agents:* Workloads where the product improves with every frontier release, requiring caution against premature cost optimization that risks falling behind competitors.

## Pricing Realities & Serving Provider Variance
* **Theoretical vs. Realized Pricing:** Static price tables fail to reflect production costs; real-world factors like cache hit rates and output token chattiness cause actual price ratios between models (e.g., GLM 52 vs. GPT 55) to diverge significantly from initial paper calculations.
* **The "Pile of Math" Engineering Gap:** Identical model weights yield vastly different production success rates depending on the provider's serving infrastructure, API configuration, and parsing logic.
* **Tool Call Reliability:** Tool call failures are driven by prosaic engineering issues—such as regular expression bugs parsing chat templates, hallucinated tool names, invalid JSON output, or mismatched parameters—rather than adversarial model degradation.

## Notable Quotes
> "The empirical usage of models is the ultimate un-gameable benchmark. Like, where are you putting your dollars? What are you using them for? And that is a very hard benchmark to game."  
> — **Chris Clark**

> "The frontier is jagged... a benchmark that simply says that one of these models is more intelligent than another, but it takes us a little while to learn these things and it takes our customers a little while to discover it and actually implement them."  
> — **Chris Clark**

> "Sometimes different providers have a bug in their regular expression and don't parse the chat templates correctly. And now all of a sudden, tool calls fail under certain circumstances... they have nothing to do with the model itself."  
> — **Chris Clark**

briefings.title: Delivering on the Promise of AI Through Trusted Partnerships | Simon Ahdoot, Hypertec | RAISE 2026
briefings.tldr: AI represents the largest civilizational infrastructure expenditure in history, requiring a decade-scale acceleration that no single institution can build alone; success depends entirely on multi-stakeholder trusted partnerships spanning compute, power, land, capital, and regional regulation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI represents the largest civilizational infrastructure expenditure in history, requiring a decade-scale acceleration that no single institution can build alone; success depends entirely on multi-stakeholder trusted partnerships spanning compute, power, land, capital, and regional regulation.

## The Scale and Opportunity of AI Infrastructure
- **Historical Comparison:** Hypertec has operated for 42 years—spanning PCs, client-server architecture, the internet, and cloud computing—but CEO Simon Ahdoot asserts that all prior IT revolutions pale in comparison to AI.
- **Societal Impact Sectors:**
  - **Healthcare:** Currently characterized as too expensive, too slow, and lacking proper visibility and results, making it ripe for AI-driven transformation.
  - **Power Grid Allocation:** Current peak-to-available power generation gaps run as high as 40% due to inefficient allocation; smarter distribution can yield massive systemic gains.
  - **Construction:** Economic output and daily workflows suffer from persistent inefficiencies (exemplified by Montreal's endless road construction); better coordination via technology can boost productivity.
- **Unprecedented Expenditure:** AI is slated to become the largest civilizational expenditure in human history, compressed into a single decade rather than the 50 to 60 years it took for electrification.

## Core Deployment Challenges
- **The Small Business Implementation Gap:** While large construction firms and enterprises can deploy AI stacks, the vast majority of companies have under five employees and lack dedicated IT staff, making full workflow integration extremely difficult beyond basic research queries.
- **Infrastructure Constraints:** 
  - **Power:** The industry is witnessing multiple gigawatt-scale power projects unlike anything seen previously in IT.
  - **Talent:** Sourcing skilled technical talent is exceptionally difficult, compounded by the monumental challenge of retraining experienced professionals to work in entirely new ways (e.g., teaching doctors with decades of practice to adopt AI-assisted workflows).
- **Public Pushback and Environmental Concerns:** Data centers face growing community opposition over high water consumption and local heat island effects (such as measured temperature increases around Arizona data centers).
- **Regional Regulatory Divergence:** Operating globally means navigating starkly different regional regulations, cultural norms, and legal frameworks where methods permitted in one jurisdiction fail in another.

## The Necessity of Ecosystem Partnerships
- **The Multi-Disciplinary Stack:** Building a single AI project requires an intricate assembly of distinct providers:
  - **Compute & Equipment:** Providers like Nvidia, Google, and AMD.
  - **Real Estate & Facilities:** Land acquisition, data center design, construction, and ongoing facility management.
  - **Infrastructure Operations:** GPU cluster management and IT infrastructure oversight (e.g., Bazz HPC).
  - **Software & Models:** Enterprise AI model developers (e.g., Cohere).
  - **Connectivity & Capital:** Enterprise networking providers, massive capital backing, and credit rating partners for long-term contract viability.
- **Hyperscaler Limitations:** Even tech hyperscalers with massive cash reserves cannot shoulder the entire capital and operational burden directly out of pocket and must rely on partner ecosystems.

## Sovereign AI and Cross-Generational Collaboration
- **The Sovereign AI Imperative:** Regional partnerships are mandatory to navigate local regulations, public trust, and physical deployments, making Sovereign AI a critical framework in markets like Canada.
- **Case Study — The Canadian Four-Way Partnership:** 
  - **Hypertec:** 42 years old (founded 1984), providing compute and IT infrastructure.
  - **Bell Canada (Bell AI Fabric):** Founded in 1880 (13 years after Canadian confederation), bringing deep institutional background and long-standing operational practices.
  - **Bazz HPC:** Founded in 2017 (9 years old), serving as the infrastructure operator running the GPU stack.
  - **Cohere:** Founded in 2019 (7 years old), supplying enterprise AI models.
- **Bridging Institutional Divorces:** The primary strategic challenge for legacy institutions (like a 140-year-old telecom) is learning to pivot and become flexible, while newer technology firms must learn how to respect and leverage centuries of institutional knowledge.

> "I heard a talk recently where somebody pointed out that artificial intelligence may be the single largest civilizational expenditure in human history... We're trying to get there within a decade." — Simon Ahdoot

> "Imagine, you have a 7-year-old, a 9-year-old, a 42-year-old, and a 140-year-old all working together. We were able to make that happen, which enables this incredible project." — Simon Ahdoot

> "If you want to be able to succeed within AI, what we're going to need to be able to do, if we want to deliver on that promise, is we need to identify the right partners, build up that trust, and get to where we can make amazing things happen together." — Simon Ahdoot

briefings.title: Elon Musk on AI: humans will no longer be in control in ten years  | The Economist
briefings.tldr: Elon Musk predicts that artificial intelligence will exceed total human intelligence in approximately five years and leave humans out of control within a decade, steering humanity toward an inevitable "age of amazing abundance."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Elon Musk predicts that artificial intelligence will exceed total human intelligence in approximately five years and leave humans out of control within a decade, steering humanity toward an inevitable "age of amazing abundance." To mitigate the residual 10–20% existential risk, he proposes a peer-review regulatory model where rival AI labs audit each other’s frontier models before government intervention.

## AI Timelines and the Future of Human Control
* **Intelligence Horizon:** **Elon Musk** estimates that AI will exceed the sum of human intelligence in roughly **5 years**, noting that there will be virtually nothing AI cannot do better than humans, aside from being human.
* **Loss of Human Control:** **Elon Musk** asserts it is unlikely humans will be in control in **10 years**, comparing the dynamic to the intelligence gap between humans and chimpanzees—noting humans are essentially evolved chimpanzees who still eat bananas.
* **The "Age of Abundance":** **Elon Musk** predicts the most likely outcome of this technological shift is an age of amazing abundance where anyone can have anything they can think of, barring a massive global thermonuclear war (World War III).
* **Inevitable Momentum:** **Elon Musk** states there is no way to stop the incredible momentum of AI and robotics, adding that even if a stop button existed, humans probably shouldn't press it because the destination is overall positive.

## Existential Risk and Philosophical Outlook
* **P-Doom Estimate:** **Elon Musk** maintains there is still a **10 to 20%** chance that killer robots and AI could mean the end of humanity.
* **Philosophical Shift:** **Elon Musk** explains that his current philosophy is to look on the bright side and "enjoy the ride," noting that in the long run, humanity faces the eventual heat death of the universe under standard physics anyway.

## Industry Self-Regulation and Peer Review

briefings.summary_markdown:
* **TL;DR:** 2CRSi CEO Alain Wilmouth and host Ethan Pierse discuss building sustainable, sovereign industrial AI infrastructure across Europe, detailing a new French consortium ("Aether") that combines immersion cooling, biomass energy, and unused agricultural land to power edge AI data centers while generating negative carbon emissions.

## The Energy & Cooling Challenge in AI Infrastructure
* **Early Pioneer in Liquid Cooling:** Alain Wilmouth noted that 2CRSi began building servers specifically for immersion cooling and Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC) in 2013 and 2015, initially supplying US universities and national labs.
* **The Cooling Energy Burden:** Historically, removing 1,000 watts of heat required spending an additional 1,000 watts on cooling. 
* **Regulatory Pressures:** Strict European regulations now enforce low Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) targets, such as ~1.3 in Germany and ~1.2 in the Netherlands.

## The Aether Consortium and Sustainable Power
* **Consortium Launch:** Announced in July 2026, "Aether" is a consortium of established industrial companies (many over 100 years old), including Dassault System, Varian, and Equans, with partners like Hafner Energy.
* **Initial Capacity:** The consortium currently has 42 megawatts available across two sites near Strasbourg, France, with a roadmap scaling up to 400 megawatts.
* **Biomass and Gasification:** To move beyond mere carbon neutrality to negative carbon footprints, the project integrates biomass energy using gasification technology via partner Hafner Energy, allowing carbon to be stored for centuries while burning cleaned wood gas.
* **Agricultural Land Integration:** Alain Wilmouth pointed out that France has 15 million hectares of land, of which 2 million hectares have been unused by farmers for at least five years. Utilizing these lands for biomass production could create approximately 250,000 jobs for struggling farmers without requiring state grants.
* **Grid Strain Concerns:** Pointing to grid constraints (such as an evening in late December when only 0.5 gigawatts of power remained available in France), Wilmouth argued against massive centralized gigawatt-scale data centers that require tens of billions in cabling, favoring decentralized edge infrastructure.

## European Sovereignty, Security, and Corporate R&D
* **Infrastructure vs. Data Sovereignty:** Beyond cloud and data sovereignty, the Aether model provides infrastructure sovereignty, allowing companies to keep their data on-premise.
* **Protection Against Geopolitical Restrictions:** Alain Wilmouth highlighted risks for European companies with partial foreign ownership (e.g., a major European car manufacturer with 32% Chinese ownership and Chinese board members blocked from buying US AI chips). 
* **Secure Enterprise AI:** The Aether model allows enterprises to run any Large Language Model (LLM) locally via black fiber connections without exposing proprietary R&D or data to cloud or LLM providers.
* **SMB Solutions:** Partnerships with companies like Goodwick and Outscale (Dassault System's Numsec Cloud) enable small and mid-sized businesses (SMBs) to maintain data security and avoid tech giants.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Roadmap to 17 AI Factories:** Alain Wilmouth stated a roadmap exists to build 17 different AI factories across Europe through partner networks owning land and power, expanding from France through Germany, Czechia, Hungary, Poland, and Romania.
* **Space-bound Servers:** Alain Wilmouth revealed that 2CRSi has already validated three servers specifically designed for space operations over the past three years.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The reality is if you imagine tomorrow that the AI will replace hundreds or millions of job everywhere in the worlds, you have to understand that if the AI is eating all the power available in countries, what will do the rest of the humanity? ... Having today the reflection, when the money is really here... we have to use it not just to make it in our pocket, but really to have a long-term view of how the AI can help to resolve the climate changing."* — **Alain Wilmouth**

> *"More you will do edge data centers, not small edge, but real edge 10, 20, 50 megawatts locally, not just three sites, but probably 30 site, interconnect with fast fiber, that is something where you can say, 'I made my service local.'"* — **Alain Wilmouth**

> *"This is not innovation just for innovation's sake. It's about seeing a version of a future that we want, applying innovation to it, and making it happen."* — **Ethan Pierse**

briefings.title: Fast, Efficient Inference at Scale with Heterogeneous Hardware | Gimlet Labs x d-Matrix | RAISE 2026
briefings.tldr: Gimlet Labs is building the industry's first multi-silicon inferencing cloud to decompose AI workloads and allocate them across heterogeneous hardware, achieving 4x to 5x gains in both capacity and interactive performance.
briefings.summary_markdown:
1. **TL;DR**: Gimlet Labs is building the industry's first multi-silicon inferencing cloud to decompose AI workloads and allocate them across heterogeneous hardware, achieving 4x to 5x gains in both capacity and interactive performance.

## Company Vision & Approach
* **Core Value Proposition:** Gimlet Labs aims to make AI inference workloads approximately 10x more efficient by decomposing them into granular components, individual models, and layers, and routing them to the optimal hardware type.
* **The Multi-Silicon Strategy:** Rather than routing between homogeneous deployments (like NVIDIA vs. AMD), Gimlet leverages the distinct strengths of various architectures—including CPUs, GPUs, and neo-accelerators like d-Matrix, Cerebras, and LPX.
* **Analogy for Heterogeneous Computing:** Zain Asgar compares the approach to choosing the right vehicle for the job: *"If you had like a Ferrari and like a minivan... you probably would not necessarily want to drive your Ferrari to the grocery store to go grocery shopping."*

## Technical Tradeoffs & Architecture
* **Hardware Constraints:** Most hardware forces tradeoffs between compute (scaling quadratically with chip area) and memory bandwidth (scaling linearly via the chip's perimeter).
* **Balancing Workloads:** 
  * *GPUs:* Typically feature large external memory with relatively low bandwidth.
  * *SRAM-Centric Chips (d-Matrix, Cerebras, LPX):* Offer high memory bandwidth but are limited by single-chip capacity (though d-Matrix addresses this by stacking memory directly on top of compute).
* **Full-Stack Challenges:** Operating a heterogeneous cloud requires solving compatibility issues across distinct programming models (spatial vs. GPU architectures), non-NVLink networking topologies (relying on Ethernet), and data center electrical and cooling systems.

## Market Context & Target Applications
* **Industry Drivers:** A severe scarcity of data center resources combined with the rise of agentic workloads (which introduce diverse CPU and tool-call tasks) created the impetus for heterogeneous scaling.
* **Key Use Cases:** Primary customer pull is focused on **coding agents**, where delivering instantaneous, low-latency responses enables developers to iterate as fast as they can think.
* **Performance Metrics:** Gimlet's approach yields approximately a **4x to 5x increase in capacity for the same cost**, and a **4x to 5x improvement in interactive performance** for end users.

## Founder Background & Execution
* **Company Status:** Gimlet Labs has raised close to **$80 million** in a Series A round led by Menlo Ventures.
* **Leadership Team:** Co-Founder & CEO Zain Asgar is a repeat entrepreneur (previously founded Pixie Labs, acquired by New Relic), former Stanford computer science professor, NVIDIA architect, Google engineering lead, and Benchmark Capital entrepreneur-in-residence. Interviewed by Sid Sheth, Co-Founder & CEO of d-Matrix.
* **Scaling Realities:** Because true heterogeneous hardware systems do not yet exist commercially, Gimlet has been forced to become vertically integrated, building and managing its own production data center capacity.
* **Entrepreneurial Learnings:** Asgar's key takeaway from his first startup is to make high-value, high-conviction strategic bets early rather than constantly negotiating middle-ground compromises.

## Notable Quotes
> *"We take a workload, decompose it in the granular components, and even like individual models and even layers within an individual model and run it on different types of hardware."* — Zain Asgar
> 
> *"Part of working with heterogeneous hardware, and it's part of the reason we became much more of a vertically integrated NeoCloud, is that there isn't actually anybody deploying like true heterogeneous hardware today."* — Zain Asgar

briefings.title: How Supabase Became One Of The Fastest Growing DevTool Companies In The World
briefings.tldr: Supabase is an open-source, Postgres-backed database and developer tools platform founded in 2020 by Paul Copplestone, which grew from an initial open-source side project into a decacorn valued at $10B after raising a $500M round.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Supabase is an open-source, Postgres-backed database and developer tools platform founded in 2020 by Paul Copplestone, which grew from an initial open-source side project into a decacorn valued at $10B after raising a $500M round. The platform has scaled to 10 million developers across 60+ countries with 360 employees, and currently powers 60% to 90% of all AI agent-generated databases.

## Background & Early Ventures
- **Paul Copplestone (Co-founder & CEO):** Originally from New Zealand, grew up with an entrepreneur father, and spent only one brief stint in a corporate consultancy before dedicating his career entirely to startups.
- **Previous Ventures:** 
  - Startup #1: Served as CTO; did not find product-market fit, leading Paul to leave after two years over strategic disagreements with the CEO.
  - Startup #2: Incubated Supabase as a side project inside a different dev tools company for two years before officially launching it out into the market.
- **Why Postgres & Open Source:** 
  - Paul closely monitored Hacker News three times a day and noticed Postgres trending upward in popularity.
  - Chose open source due to personal philosophy and community-building values; monetization took about a year and a half to begin.

## Launch & Developer Experience
- **Early Positioning:** Initially tried a real-time Postgres engine, but growth took off only after rebranding and positioning as the "Open Source Firebase Alternative."
- **Initial Target Market:** High-growth, venture-backed startups (specifically Y Combinator companies). Approximately over 60% of every YC batch now uses Supabase, though almost no one trusted them during their own batch.
- **Time to Value Metrics:** 
  - Measured AWS RDS instance spin-up time at around 8.5 minutes.
  - Set a strict internal goal to drop their own setup time under a minute, which eventually reached roughly 5 seconds.
  - Transitioned the developer experience from a visual dashboard/SQL editor to CLIs, MCPs, and Git-backed declarative schemas designed for AI agents.

## The AI Era & Agent-Driven Scale
- **Explosive Growth (2024–2026):** 
  - Growth accelerated dramatically with the rise of AI builders and "vibe coding" tools like Bolt, Lovable, Claude Code, and Codex.
  - Monthly user metrics jumped from 6.5 million to 10 million developers, with conversion rates and user activation accelerating simultaneously despite zero traditional marketing spend.
- **Supabase for Platforms:** Built to support platforms like Lovable and Bolt; enables the automated spin-up of millions of databases. Also adapted for enterprise innovation labs to manage and monitor large volumes of databases.

## Company Operations & Culture
- **Remote-First Organization:** Employs 360 people across more than 60 countries with zero physical offices.
- **AI-Driven Documentation:** Because every decision over the past six years has been fully documented in writing across Slack and Notion, their internal AI agents possess institutional memory dating back to day one.
- **Funding & Valuation:** Raised a massive series of rounds, culminating in a **$500 million funding round at a valuation exceeding $10 billion**.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Paul Copplestone:** 60% to 90% of all new database launches are now triggered by AI agents.
- **Paul Copplestone:** The next major wave of dev tool opportunity will shift from the "build stage" (prompting and generation) to the "operate stage" (self-driving, automated database management, security patches, and uptime maintenance).

## Notable Quotes
> *"The number one reason why startups fail is they run out of money, isn't it? ... We actually looked at the numbers. Usually founders giving up. Drama. Not finding product-market fit. People usually close their companies when they still have a lot of money."* — **Paul Copplestone**

> *"By all rights, AWS should never have been able... like, we should not exist if AWS are so good. They've got way more cash than us. But we've been able to for many different reasons."* — **Paul Copplestone**

> *"Money will not solve your problems. And that's a good thing for startups as well... The cash is really just in service of all those things that would allow us to win even if we didn't have the cash."* — **Paul Copplestone**

briefings.title: IBM CEO: 'Technology Spend Will Keep Growing'
briefings.tldr: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna addressed the company's lowered full-year sales forecast—driven by a temporary CapEx slowdown and mainframe sales dip among Fortune 100 clients—while reaffirming free cash flow targets and highlighting strong enterprise demand for AI, Red Hat software, and quantum computing.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
IBM CEO Arvind Krishna addressed the company's lowered full-year sales forecast—driven by a temporary CapEx slowdown and mainframe sales dip among Fortune 100 clients—while reaffirming free cash flow targets and highlighting strong enterprise demand for AI, Red Hat software, and quantum computing.

## Mainframe Performance and Capacity Growth
- **Z17 Capacity Surge:** The current Z17 machine, launched in May 2025, has achieved **130% capacity growth** compared to the prior generation.
- **Client Adoption:** **85% of mainframe clients** are actively increasing their capacity, while 15% are optimizing.
- **Structural Value Proposition:** Addressing investor comparisons to the 1990s mainframe shift, Krishna noted that unit costs for protected, resilient, and burst-capacity workloads on the mainframe remain **5 to 15 times cheaper** than alternatives, making it an architecturally superior platform rather than a displaced technology.

## Financial Guidance, Software, and Cost Management
- **Full-Year Revenue Guidance:** IBM narrowed its full-year sales forecast to **4% to 5% growth**, depending on whether CapEx headwinds persist through September.
- **Software Portfolio Split:** **80% of the software business** operates as an annuity, consumption, and OPEX-based model growing at approximately **8%**, featuring products like Red Hat, Confluent, and HashiCorp. The remaining **20%** is CapEx-sensitive.
- **Cash Flow and EBITDA:** Over the past four years, cash flow growth has outpaced revenue at **7% to 8% to 9%** annually (driven by adjusted EBITDA), supported by productivity levers and maintaining the dividend.
- **Supply Chain Backlog:** IBM exited the second quarter with **half a billion dollars of backlog** in distributed infrastructure, storage, and Unix systems due to component demand.
- **Third-Party Spend:** Headcount has remained flat over recent years; additional efficiencies are being targeted via third-party spend rather than widespread workforce reductions.
- **Starbucks Client Relationship:** Regarding Starbucks replacing an aging 10-year-old Tririga real estate lease management tool ($2M/year client), Krishna noted that interaction-based software is easily displaced by AI agents, but expects Starbucks to remain a larger overall client next year via other IBM portfolios like HashiCorp and security.

## Macroeconomic Environment and Component Pricing
- **Global GDP and Tech Spending:** IBM relies on a projected global GDP growth rate of **2% to 3%** for the year, with technology spending tracking **3 to 4 points higher** (putting the overall tech market at **5% to 6% to 7% growth**). Consulting is expected to grow at **1% to 2% to 3%**.
- **Underlying Component Inflation:** Over the past 18 months, semiconductor memory pricing is up **3 to 4 times**, networking infrastructure is up **60% to 80%**, and fiber and connectors have also risen significantly.

## Talent and Hiring
- **College Hiring Surge:** IBM hired **3 times as many college graduates** this year compared to last year.
- **Talent Pool:** The applicant database contains roughly **20 million resumes**, shifting the internal focus from talent acquisition to career pathing and ensuring employees effectively utilize AI productivity tools.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Enterprise Tech Spend Share (Arvind Krishna):** Technology spend will grow from historical averages of 3% to **5% to 6% on average today**, and will reach **10% of every enterprise's budget by 2035**.
- **Quantum Computing Timeline & Scale (Arvind Krishna):** Quantum computing has transitioned from science to engineering; IBM will deliver a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer capable of **100 million computations by 2029**.
- **Quantum Total Addressable Market (Arvind Krishna):** By the end of the **2030s**, quantum computing will create a **$1 trillion total market opportunity** in terms of economic value.

## Notable Quotes
> "If there is a cheaper alternate for that workload, I'll sort of look at you and say that means in 5 to 15 years it will move off. But that's not the case. Right now for the workloads that are on, we can show the clients that it's 5 to 15 times cheaper to keep it on the mainframe than not."
> — Arvind Krishna, CEO of IBM

> "I think technology spend is going to become a larger and larger part of every enterprise's budget... I will not be surprised if by 2035, it's 10% of everyone's budget."
> — Arvind Krishna, CEO of IBM

> "When things are 2 years away, I wouldn't call them a moonshot. I think quantum is now in the engineering realm as opposed to the science realm for the next 5 years."
> — Arvind Krishna, CEO of IBM

briefings.title: Jensen Huang says the AI doomers have it wrong
briefings.tldr: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed extreme warnings about artificial intelligence as "complete nonsense," arguing that AI is driving unprecedented productivity and net job creation rather than eliminating human labor.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed extreme warnings about artificial intelligence as "complete nonsense," arguing that AI is driving unprecedented productivity and net job creation rather than eliminating human labor. During an exclusive interview with Axios' Mike Allen in Fort Worth, Texas, Huang also discussed U.S.-China technology competition, the rise of open-source models, and why Wall Street fundamentally misunderstands the current infrastructure buildout.

## Geopolitical Competition & Trade with China
* **State of China Sales:** Huang stated that Nvidia's sales to China are approximately zero and advised investors to expect zero sales unless the U.S. and Chinese governments permit a return to the market.
* **Chinese AI Models:** Praised models like DeepSeek, Kimi, and GLM as excellent tools that advance the global industry. Huang rejected the misconception that Chinese models contain backdoors, noting they operate safely within isolated "sandboxes" and harnesses.
* **Open vs. Closed Models:** Argued that while closed models (like Anthropic and OpenAI) are fantastic for everyday use, open-source models are foundational for science, cybersecurity, and national security because transparency allows the global community to inspect and harden them.
* **Government Regulation:** Emphasized that regulation should focus on specific dual-use applications (such as autonomous vehicles and medicine) rather than restricting the underlying technology itself.

## Market Misconceptions & Wall Street's "CAPEX" Blindspot
* **The Stock Market Drop:** Explained that Wall Street panicked over recent Chinese open-source releases (similar to the DeepSeek reaction), incorrectly assuming free AI hurts hardware demand. Huang maintained that "free AI is great for hardware, chips, and data centers" because better models drive higher usage.
* **The New CAPEX Reality:** Acknowledged that the new IT industry requires significantly heavier capital expenditure (CAPEX) to build out the intelligence layer (AI factories and data centers), but argued this infrastructure buildout is industrially driven rather than cyclical or seasonal.
* **Lack of Demand Bubble:** Stated that the semiconductor industry needs to be 5 to 10 times larger than it is today, with current shortages across memory, storage, optical interconnects, and TSMC foundries.
* **The AI Flywheel:** Noted that an inflection point has been reached where AI is both useful and profitable—evidenced by companies gladly paying hundreds of millions for coding agents that dramatically increase productivity.

## The Jobs Narrative & Economic Reality
* **Net Job Creation:** Refuted predictions that AI will eliminate half of American jobs, presenting evidence of rising headcounts:
  * **Radiologists:** Increased by roughly 20% due to automated scans allowing doctors to see significantly more patients.
  * **Paralegals:** Increased by roughly 10% as automated case handling allowed firms to clear massive backlogs.
  * **Manufacturing:** Increased by some 50% over the last several years to build AI data centers and infrastructure.
* **Closing the Technology Divide:** Highlighted AI as the first major technology that closes the technology divide, acting as a personal coach and tutor for anyone regardless of background.
* **Small Corporate Footprint:** Shared that despite Nvidia's massive valuation, it employs only 50,000 people and aims to keep headcount "as small as possible" (projecting roughly 75,000 in a decade) compared to tech giants with six-figure headcounts.

## Robotics, Agents, and Future Timelines
* **The Robotic ChatGPT Moment:** Declared that the "ChatGPT moment" for robotics has already arrived, noting that robots can now reason through complex, multi-step physical tasks when given natural language prompts.
* **The Agentic Era:** Predicted that the computing landscape is shifting from 100 million active human users to a future dominated by 100 billion to a trillion software agents running continuously and consuming vast amounts of computer resources.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Global Open Source Ecosystem:** Huang stated that open-source models will proliferate globally, driven by American, European, Chinese, Japanese, and Indian developers, making openness foundational for security.
* **IPO Milestones:** Predicted that OpenAI and Anthropic will grow to go public and become "the most successful IPOs in human history."
* **Bubble Timeline:** Asserted that a major infrastructure bubble is very unlikely to occur within the next 5 years, while the 5-to-10-year outlook depends entirely on physical building constraints.
* **Useful Robotics Timeline:** Estimated that robots will become practically useful in the everyday lives of ordinary people within **3 to 4 years**.
* **Corporate Headcount Projection:** Projected that Nvidia's workforce will grow from its current 50,000 to approximately 75,000 employees over the next **10 years**.

## Notable Quotes
> "The fact that this is going to be the end of humanity, it's complete nonsense. The fact that this is going to destroy half of the American jobs is complete nonsense and all of the facts, all of the evidence point exactly to the opposite."
> — Jensen Huang

> "We are laying the foundations, building the infrastructure, the largest industrial infrastructure buildout in human history, so that we can build the foundation of industries in the future for the next generation. And so this is just the very beginning."
> — Jensen Huang

> "America is the greatest country in the world, full stop... because of all those great challenges, because of all those disagreements, we somehow manage to work it through."
> — Jensen Huang

briefings.title: "Not just small men" - how healthcare is failing women, and what can be done
briefings.tldr: Women spend 25% more of their lives in poor health than men—disproportionately during prime working years (ages 20 to 60)—driving a $1 trillion annual global economic loss.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Women spend 25% more of their lives in poor health than men—disproportionately during prime working years (ages 20 to 60)—driving a $1 trillion annual global economic loss. A report by the World Economic Forum and the McKinsey Health Institute outlines three cost-effective, high-return care delivery interventions in pregnancy, screening, and mental health that can close this gap and deliver a 3x to 6x return on investment.

## The Women's Health Gap: Scale and Economic Impact
* **Staggering Health Disparity:** Women spend 25% more time in poor health than men, a gap historically misattributed to end-of-life longevity but actually most pronounced during prime working years between the ages of 20 and 60.
* **Massive Economic Loss:** This health gap takes women out of the workforce, resulting in a lost trillion dollars of economic opportunity each year.
* **Proportionate Burden of Non-Gender-Specific Conditions:** While pregnancy is a major physiological stress, the majority of the health gap ties to conditions impacting both sexes disproportionately or differently, such as heart disease.
* **Heart Disease Fatality Rate:** Women are 50% more likely to die in the year following a heart attack than men, largely due to a medical history of treating female biology as "atypical."

## Three High-Impact, Cost-Effective Care Delivery Interventions
* **1. Breast Arterial Calcification via Mammograms:** 
  * Over 200 million women get mammograms annually. These images can simultaneously detect breast arterial calcification (calcium buildup in arteries), indicating future cardiovascular event risk.
  * Standardizing and annotating existing mammograms costs practically nothing additional, yet enables early cardiology referrals to avert major downstream heart events.
* **2. Pregnancy Complications as Cardiac Early Warnings:**
  * Hypertensive disorders like preeclampsia and gestational diabetes make women twice as likely to develop serious heart disease later in life.
  * Currently, health systems monitor these conditions during pregnancy but abandon proactive follow-up postpartum, allowing heart disease to surface aggressively decades later.
  * **Financial ROI:** Improving follow-up and long-term care costs **$400 to $450 per woman**, far lower than the **$100,000+** cost of treating a major cardiovascular event. In the US alone, this averts **$6 million to $25 million** in costs, representing a **3x to 5x return on investment**.
* **3. Perinatal Depression Screening and Integration:**
  * Postpartum depression impacts roughly 20% of women, but focusing solely on the postpartum period is too narrow. Evidence shows manifestation often begins earlier in pregnancy, requiring a holistic "perinatal depression" approach across the entire pregnancy and up to one year post-delivery.
  * Leveraging clinically validated screening tools integrated directly into routine prenatal care de-stigmatizes the condition and protects the health of both mother and baby.

## Systemic Barriers and the Role of AI in Healthcare
* **Siloed Health Systems:** Connecting diagnostic data across separate medical departments and budgets is challenging, which explains why these common-sense care integrations have not happened automatically.
* **The Data Foundation for AI:** While artificial intelligence garners massive enthusiasm, AI models are only as good as their underlying data. Historically, datasets (even during COVID-19) frequently failed to code for sex as a biological variable.
* **Clinical Decision Support:** True technological advancement requires clinical software tools to recognize female-specific presentation patterns (such as different heart attack symptoms) immediately upon identifying a patient as female.

## Personal Insights and Medical Education Blind Spots
* **Diagnostic Biases:** Medical schools historically failed to teach sex-based differences, falsely training clinicians that women are merely "smaller men" requiring only adjusted medication dosages.
* **Research and Diagnostics Discrepancy:** McKinsey partner research shows that conditions unique to women are diagnosed much less frequently than male-specific conditions—a disparity widened when male providers perform the diagnosis.
* **Endometriosis Neglect:** Endometriosis impacts 1 in 10 women (the exact same prevalence as diabetes), yet while diabetes has over 500 drugs in clinical development, endometriosis has zero approved drugs and only about 20 drugs in clinical development.

## Notable Quotes
> "Women spend 25% more time in poor health than men do. And many people think that that makes sense, that because women live longer than men, that they would spend more time in poor health because it's concentrated at the end of life. But actually, that big health gap happens during women's prime working years."
> — **Robin Pomeroy**

> "Investing in preventative care such as integrated screenings and standardized reporting could create health care system savings delivering a three to six times return."
> — **Lucy Perez**

> "For too long, when we thought about it is we have to adjust the dose because women on average are physically smaller than men and that takes care of it. I think fortunately, what we're seeing now is that people are understanding we're talking science. We're talking human biology."
> — **Lucy Perez**

briefings.title: Powering Agentic AI with AI-Ready Data Platforms That Turn Data Into Intelligence
briefings.tldr: Jason Hardy (VP of Storage Technology at NVIDIA) explains how the shift toward agentic AI requires enterprise storage to evolve from a static system of record into a dynamic system of context and a new data plane.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Jason Hardy (VP of Storage Technology at NVIDIA) explains how the shift toward agentic AI requires enterprise storage to evolve from a static system of record into a dynamic system of context and a new data plane. This transformation relies on AI-ready data platforms, specialized memory tiers for KV cache, and co-designed NVIDIA technologies like Vera and BlueField-4 STX working alongside storage partners.

## The Three Pillars of Enterprise Data & Agentic Demand
- **Structured Data:** Comprising small volumes from ERP systems, SQL databases, and business systems where core operational decisions are made.
- **Unstructured Data:** Representing the lion's share of enterprise volume—including home directories, SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Docs, NAS shares, PDFs, video, and audio—noted as the hardest to process due to diverse data types.
- **Agent Context (The New Category):** Encompassing KV cache, agent memory, scratchpads, to-do lists, and embeddings generated as agents consume information and execute tasks; some agents operate for hours while others persist for years.
- **New Operational Paradigm:** Storage must transition from stateless, short-lived interactions to handling long-running, 24/7 sessions where tens to thousands of agents iterate over blended structured and unstructured datasets at speeds vastly exceeding human reading rates.

## Data Preparation & The AI Data Platform
- **Overcoming Enterprise Hallucinations:** High-profile failures (Air Canada, UnitedHealth, Google, Deloitte) are fundamentally data preparation issues rather than purely AI model flaws.
- **Complex Ingestion Pipeline:** 
  - **Multimodal Ingestion:** Processing text, tables, and imagery within documents like PDFs concurrently.
  - **Cleaning & Enrichment:** Removing duplication, normalizing data, stripping out PII and sensitive data, and attaching descriptive metadata.
  - **Chunking & Vectorization:** Breaking data into semantic units, embedding them into vector databases, indexing, and governing them.
- **In-Place AI Data Platforms:** NVIDIA is collaborating with partners like Dell, NetApp, IBM, and HPE to embed AI-ready capabilities directly into enterprise storage systems at the time of creation.
- **NVIDIA Blueprints:** Utilizing the RAG blueprint to streamline vectorization and embedding, and the VSS (Video Search and Summarization) blueprint to help agents understand video context directly within the storage system.

## Memory Hierarchies and KV Cache Innovation
- **Memory Tiering Architecture:**
  - **G1 (HBM):** Fastest memory directly inside the GPU, holding active KV cache and model weights.
  - **G2 (System Memory):** Tightly coupled memory collaborating with HBM for model staging and spillover.
  - **G3 (Scratch):** NVMe disk inside each server for operating systems.
  - **G3.5 (CMX):** A new dedicated tier introduced by NVIDIA specifically for KV cache management, sitting between high-performance storage and GPU memory.
  - **G4 (High-Performance Storage):** Traditional high-performance storage, object storage, and enterprise storage where models live and checkpointing occurs.
- **KV Cache Efficiency:** CMX stores and serves prefill and decode stage token computations so GPUs spend zero time recomputing existing cached data, maximizing token-per-second output across the AI factory.

## Hardware Foundations & Co-Design
- **Vera CPU Integration:** Designed to take bits, bytes, and packets off the wire and feed them to the GPU with 3x memory bandwidth and best-in-class single-threaded performance, directly benefiting storage workloads.
- **NVIDIA Vera BlueField-4 STX Platform:** An opinionated storage design acting as the foundation for the AI factory, combining NVIDIA software, Vera/BlueField-4 STX hardware, and storage partner ecosystems.
- **Horizontal & Vertical Co-Design:** Integrating network (Spectrum-X), compute (Vera), GPUs (Rubin/RTX Pro), and storage platforms to scale agentic AI safely while maintaining enterprise trust, security, compliance, and hybrid on-prem/cloud governance.

## Notable Quotes
> "Storage needs to move from being what we've known as a system of record to now a system of context."
> — Jason Hardy

> "If you don't address the data accurately, if you don't bring the right data to the context, things can go a little sideways... This isn't an AI issue. This is a data issue."
> — Jason Hardy

> "Every enterprise, every AI factory needs an AI data platform... It's about taking that data, preparing it at the edge at the time of creation in the storage system, and taking that refined good and bringing it to the AI factory so that I can manufacture intelligence."
> — Jason Hardy

## TL;DR
President Trump announced that over 220 entities have signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, requiring major tech companies and AI data centers to fund or build their own energy infrastructure to prevent consumer rate hikes while keeping the U.S. ahead in AI and manufacturing.

## Ratepayer Protection Pledge and Energy Infrastructure
* **Self-Funded Tech Infrastructure:** 
  * Large tech companies and AI data centers are formally committing to fund or build all required energy infrastructure rather than passing costs to consumers.
  * AI data centers and big tech are essentially becoming their own utilities and building dedicated power plants because current electricity demand is more than double current production levels.
* **Pledge Adoption and Rate Protections:** 
  * Over 220 utilities, tech companies, state governments, and partners have signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge since its introduction a few months ago.
  * Electricity rates for 80% of power distributed in America are currently kept in check by the plan.
* **Specific Utility and State Impacts:**
  * **Georgia Power:** Froze base rates for households until 2029; revenue from Google's data center construction is allowing the elimination of property taxes entirely (noted by Gov. Brian Kemp).
  * **American Electric Power (AEP):** Projects $16 billion in cost offsets for consumers through data center contracts.
  * **Alliant Energy (Iowa):** Data center deals allow them to freeze electric rates for consumers for at least 5 years.
  * **Meta Project (Richland Parish, Louisiana):** A $27 billion project provides public school teachers with up to $50,000 in bonuses this year and saves local residents $2.6 billion on electricity bills (noted by Sheldon Jones).

## Economic Boom, Investments, and Trade
* **Foreign and Domestic Investment Metrics:** 
  * $19.2 trillion in investments have poured into the U.S. in the last 12 months, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs (compared to less than $1 trillion in 4 years under the previous administration).
* **Automotive and Manufacturing Growth:** 
  * Toyota is moving its operations from Mexico to the U.S.
  * The U.S. is building more car plants currently than at any time in history following years of zero new plant construction.
* **Semiconductor Market Progress:** 
  * The U.S. is projected to capture about 50% of the chip market by the end of the current term, up from virtually none (excluding Intel) at the start of the initiative.
  * An investment in 10% of Intel yielded approximately a $72 billion profit, with Intel's stock price having gone up "many times."

## Artificial Intelligence and Global Competition
* **AI Dominance Goals:** 
  * President Trump stated that AI is bigger than the internet or anything seen thus far, and whoever wins the AI race wins overall.
  * The U.S. is currently leading China and all other countries by a lot in AI and crypto.
* **International Dynamics:** 
  * Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit Washington on September 24th to discuss trade and technology.
  * Foreign nations and lobbyists are spending money on propaganda and PR to convince communities to reject data centers and slow down U.S. progress.

## Military, Foreign Policy, and Current Operations
* **Iran Conflict Status:** 
  * U.S. military operations against Iran have knocked out their navy, air force, radar, and manufacturing capability.
  * Iranian drone capacity is down 84% and missile capacity is down 91%; all 159 ships and 212 airplanes have been neutralized.
* **Venezuela Operations:** 
  * Operations in Venezuela were completed in a "one-day war" at a profit where the U.S. is taking millions of barrels of oil to Houston and Louisiana, paying for the conflict many times over while Venezuelan oil companies generate record earnings.
* **Casualties:** 
  * Four American service members were recently killed, bringing total recent casualties across two conflicts to 18.

## Key Attendees and Administration Recognition

* **Governors in Attendance:** Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry, Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen, Idaho Governor Brad Little, and Georgia Governor Brian Kemp.
* **Industry Executives and Community Leaders:** Entergy CEO Drew Marsh, Southern Company CEO Chris Womack, Meta President Dena Powell, Columbia County Commission Chairman Doug Duncan, and Richland Parish School District's Sheldon Jones.

## Notable Quotes
> "Under this groundbreaking plan, America's largest tech companies have formally committed to fund or build all energy infrastructure required to meet the demand they are placing on the grid."
> — President Donald Trump

> "Revenue from Google's data center construction is allowing them to eliminate property taxes entirely. And that's what you call using it to your advantage."
> — President Donald Trump

> "They have no military, they have no Navy... every one [of their 159 ships] is at the bottom of the sea. They have 212 airplanes, every one is gone."
> — President Donald Trump

briefings.title: Sovereign Stacks: Building Trusted AI on National Terms | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Sovereignty in AI is about maintaining practical control, choice, and a "Plan B" across the infrastructure stack rather than pursuing complete isolation or relying purely on regulatory compliance checkboxes.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
Sovereignty in AI is about maintaining practical control, choice, and a "Plan B" across the infrastructure stack rather than pursuing complete isolation or relying purely on regulatory compliance checkboxes. Addressing these challenges requires balancing massive infrastructure scale (such as $100 billion compute demands) with open ecosystems and pragmatic business realities.

---

### Defining Sovereign AI: Control vs. Isolation
* **Pragmatic Goals over Paperwork:** Gleb Budman (Backblaze) noted that sovereignty is frequently confused with regulatory paperwork or mere residency, arguing that true sovereignty is the pragmatic ability for an organization to manage, move, and access its data and workflows without punitive taxes like egress fees.
* **Control, Not Autarchy:** Mohsen Moazami (DDN / ex-Groq) emphasized that sovereignty is about control and avoiding single-vendor hostage situations, not isolation, pointing out that Saudi Arabia achieved sovereign compute stack control while successfully exporting tokens.
* **Vendor Independence:** Thomas Di Giacomo (SUSE) defined sovereignty as the freedom to exit, pivot, and maintain choice, pointing to open-source software as a critical mandate supported by the European Commission to prevent vendor lock-in.
* **Business Enabler:** Simon Muskett (Digital Realty) described infrastructure platforms as the foundational enabler of sovereign decisions, where data location, security, and network architecture directly dictate business outcomes.

### Navigating the AI Stack and Infrastructure Realities
* **Cross-Stack Interdependence:** Simon Muskett highlighted that all layers of the stack—from data centers and cooling (such as Digital Realty's Paris partnership with Mistral) to networking and models—are equally critical, requiring holistic design rather than focusing solely on frontier models.
* **Risk Mitigation and Plan B:** Thomas Di Giacomo argued that infrastructure layers (like hardware and cloud foundations) require a dual-vendor or backup strategy because failure at this layer halts mission-critical business operations.
* **Granular Enterprise Use Cases:** Corey Hawkvelt (Hyperstack) explained that enterprise AI sovereignty is not "carte blanche"; an enterprise may route low-sensitivity tasks (like marketing cat memes) to the cheapest global provider while keeping sensitive finance data under strict local compliance.
* **Global Scale Disconnect:** Mohsen Moazami contrasted European neo-clouds operating at scales of 10,000 GPUs due to 3-year depreciation risks with American model companies handling single-customer purchase orders worth **$100 billion** in compute.
* **Tokenomics and Efficiency:** Simon Muskett noted that tokenomics, latency, and liquid cooling requirements—costing hundreds of millions or billions of dollars—drive modern GPU placement and infrastructure profitability.

### Geopolitical Pressures and Innovation Trade-Offs
* **Engineers Under Constraints:** Corey Hawkvelt argued that US foreign policy and export controls act as a positive catalyst for business and engineering innovation, forcing nations like China to build competitive indigenous models and hardware (such as Huawei GPUs).
* **The Rise of "Buy Europe":** Thomas Di Giacomo observed that while Europe has historically lagged and been shy about national procurement preferences, a "buy Europe" mindset is emerging, which can successfully revitalize European technology sectors.
* **Interdependence as a Pre-requisite:** Gleb Budman compared data infrastructure to airports: *“The only reason that any of those are valuable is because the planes fly between them,”* warning that hyper-restricted data residency without cross-border mobility renders data useless.

---

### Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Obsolescence of the Term:** Thomas Di Giacomo predicts that by 2030 or 2035, the specific word "sovereignty" will no longer be discussed because the underlying concepts of control and independence will have matured.

---

### Notable Quotes
> *"Sovereignty is not about isolation, it's about control... there is no equivalent of NVIDIA anywhere on the planet."*  
> — **Mohsen Moazami**

> *"That sovereignty is residency. I mean, fundamentally, just because you put some... just because you put the airport here, if the planes don't fly anywhere, you have nothing."*  
> — **Gleb Budman**

> *"Sovereignty cannot be enforced by regulations. The business and technology will drive the adoption."*  
> — **Thomas Di Giacomo**
